reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: A mistuned (1.8 kHz) passive membrane-cell wall has no demonstrated friction benefit; Kramer-type membrane coatings never reproduced drag reduction reliably, and cell dimpling can add slight roughness, so 0% versus a clean foul-release coating.
key_assumption_issues: Simulated 45% is fouling detachment stress, not drag.
Foundation stiffness G_gel/h ignores the incompressibility of a confined gel; a sealed gel cell is far stiffer in the normal direction, which could remove most of the compliance advantage.
Mean compliance over a cell averages rigid septa lines with compliant centres; barnacles spanning several cells feel the stiff septa.
killer_risks: Membrane-septa joints fatigue under ~1e10 pressure cycles per year and let seawater into cells.
Cuts or punctures expose gel-filled cells; the gel washes out or swells.
Paneling or laminating a cellular film on curved hull areas is costly and slow.

requirement_coverage.name: non_toxic_antifouling
requirement_coverage.reason: Biocide-free, easier release than standard foul release if cells stay compliant; stiff septa lines weaken it.

requirement_coverage.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirement_coverage.reason: Tough skin helps abrasion, but joint fatigue and water ingress are long-term risks.

requirement_coverage.name: hull_scale_applicability
requirement_coverage.reason: Requires manufactured cellular panels or films, not a paint.

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The concept does not alter near-wall turbulence measurably (dissipation ~0.02% of production), so clean-hull friction equals a standard foul-release coating; the 68% is a fouling-release stress reduction.
key_assumption_issues: Metric is fouling detachment stress, not drag.
1D series-shear compliance ignores crust bending and peel mechanics; real release depends on the barnacle size relative to the crust bending length.
Adhesion work of the crust (0.06 J/m2) assumed close to PDMS.
killer_risks: Crust/gel delamination under impact: gel cohesive strength is very low, so blisters and tears appear after fender contact.
Once the crust is cut, the exposed gel is destroyed by cleaning and flow.
Thick (~2.8 mm) multi-layer silicone build costs several times a standard foul-release system.
Microfouling slime still forms at low speed.

requirement_coverage.name: non_toxic_antifouling
requirement_coverage.reason: Biocide-free with very low release stress; no settlement prevention.

requirement_coverage.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirement_coverage.reason: Crust fixes abrasion of the gel surface but introduces a weak crust/gel interface.

requirement_coverage.name: hull_scale_applicability
requirement_coverage.reason: Sprayable multi-layer system, but thick and costly with tight thickness control.
